Command: A priest shall not serve with torn garments
Summary: The command: A priest shall not serve with torn garments (Leviticus 10:6). Aaron and his sons were not to tear their garments in mourning while the anointing oil was upon them.
Commandment: A priest shall not serve with torn garments.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: Aaron and his sons were not to tear their garments in mourning while the anointing oil was upon them — a ceremonial law about the priest in grief. Its goal was to keep the priests in service even while the dead lay before them: the oil was upon them, and mourning's signs were forbidden during the work. The evil was grief breaking the order of worship, the priest's mourning tearing the garments of his office. It restrained that by holding the garments whole: the priest served with his clothes intact.
